## Getting UNICEF MICS files {#c01-unicef}

UNICEF releases MICS microdata as SPSS (`.sav`) files. The files already carry variable and value labels, so you can open them in R or Stata without a separate codebook.

### Download the country files

1.  Open <https://mics.unicef.org/surveys>.
2.  Log in if the site asks you to. Dataset downloads usually need an account.
3.  Filter to the surveys you want: round **MICS6**, then region or countries, data type **MICS**, and status **Completed**.
4.  Click **Download MICS datasets**. UNICEF packs every matching survey into one bulk zip, usually named `MICS_Datasets.zip`.

Create a project folder in your local computer, for example `MICS project`, and save `MICS_Datasets.zip` in it.

### Unpack with AFLEARN's scripts

The `MICS_Datasets.zip` bulk zip nests each country survey in further archives and wrapper folders, as shown in the illustration below. Unpacking a large number of country surveys by hand wastes time and invites path errors.

``` text
MICS_Datasets.zip
└── survey folder
    └── another archive
        └── wrapper folder
            ├── fs.sav
            ├── hh.sav
            └── ...
```

To avoid this, firstly download from [AFLEARN's repository](https://github.com/datafirst-aflearn/mics-guide/raw/main/Script.zip) `Script.zip` and unzip it into the same project folder, i.e., `MICS project`, so `Script/` sits beside `MICS_Datasets.zip`. See blow:

``` text
MICS project/
├── MICS_Datasets.zip
└── Script/
```

Next, open R, set the `MICS project` folder as the working directory and source `run-it.R` as shown below:

```{r eval=FALSE}
setwd("C:/path/to/MICS project")
source("Script/run-it.R")
```

You have to ascertain that the working directory must be the folder that holds `Script/`. After a successful run, you will notice that there is now a `Data/` folder with a `UNICEF/` folder inside that carries all the unpacked and tidy country surveys you would have downloaded. Each survey then has a predictable path such as `Data/UNICEF/BEN_2021_MICS6_v01_M/fs.sav`.

``` text
MICS project/
├── MICS_Datasets.zip
├── Script/
└── Data/
    ├── UNICEF/
    │   ├── BEN_2021_MICS6_v01_M/
    │   │   ├── fs.sav
    │   │   ├── hh.sav
    │   │   ├── hl.sav
    │   │   └── ...
    │   └── ...
    └── AFLEARN Harmonised Data/
       
```

You will also notice a folder called `AFLEARN Harmonised Data/`. This folder carried the AFLEARN harmonised microdata file, which will be explained in depth in Chapter 3 on Harmonising MICS6 microdata.

::: alternativebox-header
**Keep the original download**
:::

::: alternativebox
Keep the original `MICS_Datasets.zip` file. The clean country survey folders are for analysis, while the `MICS_Datasets.zip` file is the unchanged source.
:::
